subject.title: [Bug]: Gateway heap grows to 1073MB+ at idle on macOS, cron jobs fail silently under memory pressure (ref #86613, #86509)

question: Should cron failure reporting for started-but-no-terminal-state runs remain best-effort inside Gateway plus restart recovery, or should OpenClaw add a supervisor/restart-aware lifecycle path that can alert when Gateway is wedged?
rationale: Source shows current alerts are emitted from the same Gateway process that the report says becomes starved, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add durable lifecycle alerting
options.body: Track cron started/success/error state durably and surface timeout/interruption alerts from a restart-aware or supervisor-visible path that does not depend solely on the wedged turn completing.

options.title: Require soak proof before changing architecture
options.body: Keep the current in-process alert design unless a current-main macOS launchd soak reproduces silent started-without-terminal-state cron failures after the watcher and recovery mitigations.

options.title: Split memory and cron reliability
options.body: Track the memory backend pressure and cron alert architecture as separate canonical issues if maintainers want narrower ownership and validation paths.

recommendation.title: Add durable lifecycle alerting
recommendation.body: Track cron started/success/error state durably and surface timeout/interruption alerts from a restart-aware or supervisor-visible path that does not depend solely on the wedged turn completing.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron startup/recovery work makes yetval the strongest available owner signal for the lifecycle-state part of the decision.
